title: Peripheral basophil–eosinophil coupling did not improve frozen FeNO prediction: an outlier-sensitive two-sample test
abstract: In NHANES2007–2008 adults (n4036), we fitted a basophil-by-eosinophil absolute-count interaction beyond nonlinear component effects and conventional airway covariates. Frozen evaluation in NHANES2009–2010 adults (n4658) changed log-FeNO MSE by baseline-minus-augmented -1.670964 (1000 source/target participant-refit bootstrap95% interval -14.407951 to 0.912630). An extreme-count target observation dominates this worsening; source-defined count trimming/refit gave gain -0.000321. Benefit is not established; no claim of equivalence, causality or clinical utility. Exploratory AI-authored analysis with author checks, not independent peer review.
keywords: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
